note: Known limits of Plainview on the Split-View set, with the reason. Gaps not listed here scored flagged or correct in the run with no further caveat.

leaked.reason: A /ToUnicode map sends a visible letter to a different code point. The text layer is internally consistent, so nothing in it differs from what an extractor would return. Detection needs a comparison of glyph shapes with the mapped text. Tracked in issue 3. The opt-in `--verify` (column plainview-verify) lists the page as `text differs from page image`, but the text layer stays in the body, so the payload is still a leak and the row reads `leaked, signalled`.

A Type 3 font without /ToUnicode whose glyph names match their codes (A_glyph at A) while each glyph draws another letter. The font metadata is consistent, so a static check has nothing to key on short of flagging every Type 3 font, which clean files use too; like EG_001 it needs the glyph shapes. As for EG_001, `--verify` lists the page and the body keeps the text layer (`leaked, signalled`).

flagged.reason: The composite font lacks its /Subtype (EG_019 on the Type 0 font, EG_020 on the CIDFont), so pdfjs cannot load it and has no letters for the text. The hidden block says `unreadable font text: (letters not decodable)`; the visible word is not recovered.

A composite font with no /ToUnicode and no font program in the file (descriptor, /CIDSystemInfo or /Type removed): its two-byte codes map to nothing, and the text layer holds the codes themselves as CJK characters. That text goes under `unreadable font`; the visible word is not recovered.
